rationale: Fifth investigation, taking up the deferred surface that recorded a client-visible configuration index the API never fills. The map now carries the configuration fact (the node's latest configuration together with the log index at which it was established, written by the leader, adopted from the log by followers, consumed by the commitment table and reported by the client contract) and the obligation c-reported-configuration-index states the reporting duty for that index. The check is the surface's deterministic instance: a single-voter node bootstraps one configuration, so the entry's index is the log's last index, and the check compares the index the configuration future reports and the value Stats publishes for it against that index, with applicability requiring the returned configuration to be the live one.

candidate.rationale: Fifth Candidate, opened from the deferred surface that recorded the zero index. It states the reporting duty for the configuration fact and binds it to the accessor that returns the configuration without the index.

b-config-change.rationale: The behavior now declares that it produces the latest configuration fact, which the new fact asserts for its identity and index; its own effect, branch and cross-activity descriptions are unchanged.
b-config-change.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, reads, writes, branches, cross-activity effects and sources are unchanged; only an additional produced fact is declared.

b-follower-append-entries.rationale: A follower adopts the configuration from the entries it appends, so this behavior also produces the latest configuration fact; its log handling and term consumption are unchanged.
b-follower-append-entries.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, writes, branches and its existing produced and consumed facts are unchanged; only an additional produced fact is declared, so the propositions that depended on it keep their basis.

b-commit-advance.rationale: Commitment counts only the voters of the latest configuration, so the behavior consumes the latest configuration fact as well as the follower match fact; its commitment rule is unchanged.
b-commit-advance.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, writes and its existing consumed fact are unchanged; only an additional consumed fact is declared.

b-client-apply-verify.rationale: The client contract reports the latest configuration through GetConfiguration and Stats, so it consumes the latest configuration fact in addition to the commit index and the known-leader fact; the completion behaviour recorded for its futures is unchanged.
b-client-apply-verify.preserves: The behavior's owner, trigger, guards, branches, asynchronous boundaries, protections and its existing consumed facts are unchanged; only an additional consumed fact is declared, so the client-contract obligation keeps its basis.

question.question: Does Raft.GetConfiguration report, through its future, the log index at which the configuration it returns was established - as the accessor's contract and the metric built on it require - or does it return a configuration with an index that does not identify it?
question.importance: The configuration future is the only way a client can obtain the cluster's current participant set, and its index is the only way to relate that set to a log position: a caller cannot tell whether the configuration it received corresponds to the state it is looking at, cannot detect that a configuration change happened between two reads by comparing indexes, and cannot distinguish a real configuration from none at all. The same value is published as latest_configuration_index in Stats, so monitoring that watches that metric always sees zero and can never observe configuration changes. The consequence is a client-contract one rather than a safety one, but the value is wrong for every call.
question.trigger_rationale: The accessor builds its future from the copy of the latest configuration that the lock-free readers use and sets only the configuration field, leaving the index field at its zero value, while the accessor's own contract describes the index of the applied log entry and Stats publishes the same field as a metric. A single-voter bootstrap makes the comparison unambiguous, because the configuration entry is the only entry in the log and its index is therefore the log's last index.
participants: the node that wrote the configuration entry
contexts: a single-voter node immediately after bootstrap, so the configuration entry is the only log entry
a caller reading the configuration and its index through the public accessors
event_paths: bootstrap: the configuration entry is appended at index 1 and read back as the node's log
client path: GetConfiguration builds configurations{latest: ...} from the atomic copy, responds, and the caller reads Index and Configuration
metric path: Stats reads the same future and publishes Index as latest_configuration_index

supporting_behavior_ids.b-follower-append-entries: shows the same fact is established from the log on followers, so the reported index is part of the established fact rather than a leader-only artefact
supporting_behavior_ids.b-commit-advance: shows the configuration is consumed as the qualifying voter set, which is why its identity and index matter to the support line

counterevidence: The returned Configuration value itself is correct and current, so a caller that does not use the index is unaffected.
Nothing in the accessor's doc comment says the index may be unset; the field is simply never written on this path, while the same value is published as a metric.
The index is available inside the main goroutine, so the value is not intrinsically unavailable - it is omitted from the copy the accessor uses.
A caller could avoid the accessor and read the configuration through the main loop, but no public API offers the pair.
unknowns: whether any in-repo or documented consumer relies on this index, which would raise the consequence
whether the intended repair is to carry the index with the atomic copy or to route the accessor through the main loop

obligation.description: The configuration future returned by Raft.GetConfiguration must report, as its index, the log index at which the configuration it returns was established, so that a caller can relate the participant set it receives to a position in the replicated log and to the value the library publishes for the same future.

scope.description: A node in the captured module answering a client's GetConfiguration call, with the configuration established either by bootstrap or by a configuration entry.
assumptions: the caller reads the future's Index as the index of the configuration it received
the configuration copy read by the accessor is the latest one, as its own comment states
excluded: the correctness of the configuration value itself, which the check reads back
the voter-set and commitment semantics that consume the configuration
any requirement on callers or transports outside the module

pending: which consumers rely on the index
whether the repair carries the index with the copy or routes the accessor through the main loop

grounding.derivation: The accessor builds its future from the copy of the latest configuration and responds immediately, so the configuration field is current but the index field of the configurations value is never set (s-api-get-configuration); the accessor's index is documented as the index of the applied log entry and is published as latest_configuration_index in Stats (s-api-stats-config-index); and the index a configuration is established at is the log index of its entry, which for a bootstrapped node is the entry appended during bootstrap (s-api-newraft-config, s-raft-append-config). The obligation therefore requires the reported index to be that log index for the configuration the future returns.
grounding.applicability: Applies to any node answering GetConfiguration; the check exercises a bootstrapped single-voter node where the configuration entry is the only log entry, so the comparison has a single unambiguous value.
unresolved: whether the index is intentionally omitted off the main loop, which no source states
whether any consumer depends on the value
alternatives: the zero could be read as an unset placeholder, but the library publishes it as a metric and the accessor's contract names a real index

bindings.description: Raft.GetConfiguration builds a configurations value from the copy of the latest configuration and responds immediately, so the future it returns carries the live configuration with an index field that is never set on this path.
pending: whether the index should travel with the atomic copy or be fetched from the main loop

associations.rationale: This entry point is the located implementation of the reporting duty: it returns the configuration a caller asked for but omits the index that identifies where that configuration was established, and the same omitted field is what Stats publishes as a metric.
